newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Alumbrera biggest ever base metal start-up - MIM.
newsitem.headline: Alumbrera biggest ever base metal start-up - MIM.

text.p: MIM Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday the Alumbrera mine in Argentina, due to start production in August-September, would be the world's biggest base metal mine ever started.
"I believe it (Alumbrera) will be the biggest base metal mine ever to have been started - others have grown larger but from smaller first stages," MIM chief executive Nick Stump said in a speech.
Stump said the mine would have an annual production averaging 180,000 tonnes of copper and 640,000 ounces of gold.
This would rise to 190,000 tonnes of copper and 730,000 ounces of gold by 2000, he said.
"Alumbrera in the year 2000 is expected to rank ninth among world copper mines and fourteenth among gold mines," Stump said.
Alumbrera's copper-gold concentrate was a clean product with most of the production already committed under long-term frame contracts ranging up to eight years, Stump said.
"At today's metal prices it will generate about US$600 million to US$700 million in revenue in the year 2000," he said.
"It will be at the bottom end of the copper cost curve when gold credits are taken into account," Stump said.
MIM has a 50 percent stake in the project.
Australia's North Ltd and Canada's Rio Algom Ltd have 25 percent each.
